claims.claim_ar: اختصار لفظي في تركيب جوابِ لَوْ / لَـ يبيّن إيجاز العبارة وحذف عناصر لفظية دالّة على المعنى الضمني
claims.claim_en: Conciseness (i'jaaz): a lexical omission/ellipses (described as 'اختصار لفظي') shortens the expression and leaves part of the meaning implicit, increasing terseness and force.
claims.needs_review_reason: Zamakhshari's discussion refers to omission of the lam/particles in answers generally; applying this to this specific particle (لَوْلَا) should be checked against other exegeses and readings.

claims.claim_ar: التفات في وجه الخطاب: تغيير المقصود من المخاطب (من الرسول/عامّ المخاطبين إلى الكفرة) لرفع حدة التوبيخ والتحذير.
claims.claim_en: Iltifat (shift of address): a change in the addressee or the orientation of the discourse (noted as 'على طريقة الالتفات'), which sharpens reproach and draws attention to the threatened party.

claims.claim_ar: أسلوب بلاغي حكم: صيغة شرطية استنكاريّة (نمط جحود/إنكار قوي) تُستخدم لبيان موقف المكذبين ولتسليط الضوء على عاقبة إنكار الحق.
claims.claim_en: Asloob hakim (stylistic mode): a powerful style of denial/reproach (described as 'أسلوب من الجحود بليغ')—the hypothetical/conditional formulation functions rhetorically to expose the deniers and justify the warning.

warnings: All claims are drawn only from the supplied source chunks (mainly Zamakhshari). Other classical commentators (al-Jurjani, al-Sakkaki, al-Baqillani, al-Suyuti, tafsir balagha) were not present in the provided chunks, so relevant devices from those authors may be missing.

Some identifications (e.g., treating the discussed omission as 'ijaaz' tied to the particle لَوْلَا) require cross-checking against other readings and grammatical analyses; see 'needs_review_reason' for details.

Source quotes are exact substrings from the provided chunks; claims relate the quoted commentary to the ayah-level rhetoric and may summarize the commentator's general remark as applied to this verse.
